exercises.name: Air Squat
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes turned out slightly.
Send the hips back and down while the chest stays tall and the knees follow the toes.
Lower until the hip crease drops below the top of the knees with the heels flat.
Drive through the whole foot and stand until hips and knees are fully straight.
exercises.formCue: Hip crease below the knee, then stand all the way up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Cutting the depth short, or letting the knees cave in and the heels lift as the weight shifts to the toes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Squat to a box or bench set just below knee height and stand from there.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A full-depth, fully-locked-out squat is the standard every loaded squat and thruster is built on.

exercises.name: Barbell Thruster
instructions: Hold the bar in the front rack with a full grip just outside the shoulders and elbows up in front of the bar.
Squat until the hip crease is below the knees while the chest and elbows stay high.
Stand up hard and let the drive from the legs lift the bar off the shoulders.
Press only after the hips and knees are straight, and lock the bar out over the middle of the foot.
Bring the bar back to the shoulders before you start the next squat.
exercises.formCue: Legs first, arms last.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing before the legs have finished extending, or starting the next squat before the bar is back on the shoulders.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use dumbbells or an empty bar and squat to a ball or box to learn the depth.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the legs and arms to share one lift, which makes it one of the most demanding conditioning movements with a barbell.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift High Pull
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, traps, upper back, shoulders
instructions: Stand wider than shoulder width with the bar over midfoot and grip it with both hands inside the knees.
Set a flat back with the chest up and the arms straight.
Push the floor away and keep the bar close until the hips and knees are fully extended.
Shrug, then pull the elbows high and out until the bar reaches about collarbone height.
Lower in reverse order: arms straighten first, then the hips and knees bend.
exercises.formCue: Stand tall first, then elbows high and outside.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the arms before the hips open, or rounding the lower back off the floor.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a single light kettlebell and stop the pull at chest height.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the hips-then-arms sequence that every clean, snatch and medicine-ball clean depends on.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Clean
instructions: Stand over the ball with feet shoulder-width apart, squat down with the chest up and place a palm on each side of the ball.
Stand up with straight arms until the hips and knees are fully open.
Shrug hard, then drop under the ball right away and turn the hands beneath it.
Catch it at the shoulders in the bottom of a squat with the elbows up.
Stand to full height before lowering the ball for the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Jump, shrug, drop under.
exercises.commonMistakes: Curling the ball up with the arms, or pulling before the hips have fully opened.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a very light ball and catch in a shallow squat until the timing is smooth.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the pull-under of the clean with a load that is safe to miss.

exercises.name: Kipping Pull-Up
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, biceps, shoulders, abs, hip flexors
instructions: Hang with arms straight, hands just outside the shoulders and the shoulders pulled slightly away from the ears.
Swing from the shoulders between an arched position with the chest forward and a hollow position with the feet forward.
As the body rises out of the hollow, pull with the arms until the chin clears the bar.
Push away from the bar at the top and fall back into the arch to load the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Swing from the shoulders, then pull late.
exercises.commonMistakes: Driving the swing with the legs instead of the shoulders, or dropping from the top with loose shoulders.
exercises.beginnerModification: Build strict pull-ups first, then practise kip swings alone without the pull.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Using the whole body lets you do more pulling work in less time once strict strength is in place.

exercises.name: Chest-to-Bar Pull-Up
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, rhomboids, rear delts, biceps, abs
instructions: Hang with straight arms and start a controlled kip swing from the shoulders.
Out of the hollow position, drive the hips up and pull the elbows down and back.
Keep pulling until the chest touches the bar below the collarbone.
Push away from the bar and return to a full hang before the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Pull the bar to your sternum, elbows behind you.
exercises.commonMistakes: Stopping at chin height, or reaching with the chin and neck instead of pulling the elbows back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do strict or kipping pull-ups to the chin, or ring rows pulled all the way to the chest.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The longer pull builds the height and upper-back strength that bar muscle-ups need.

exercises.name: Kipping Bar Muscle-Up
instructions: Hang with straight arms and build a strong kip swing from arch to hollow.
From the back of the swing, drive the hips toward the bar while pulling it down toward the waist with straight-ish arms.
As the hips rise, sit the chest fast over the bar so the shoulders end up above the hands.
Press out to straight arms in the support position.
Lower with control and push away from the bar to re-enter the swing.
exercises.formCue: Hips to the bar, then chest over fast.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling with bent arms too early so the hips never rise, or landing on one elbow at a time.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work strict pull-ups, chest-to-bar pull-ups and bar dips, and practise the turnover by jumping from a box.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It links a pull and a dip into one movement that takes you from hanging below the bar to supported above it.

exercises.name: Toes-to-Bar
instructions: Hang with straight arms and start a small kip swing from arch to hollow.
As you move into the hollow, press down on the bar with the lats and lift both feet together.
Touch both feet to the bar at the same time between the hands.
Pull the feet back and down while the chest moves forward into the arch, ready for the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Push the bar down, bring the toes up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the legs drop loosely so the swing gets wild, or bending the arms to reach the bar.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do hanging knee raises, or alternate one leg at a time toward the bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the trunk and lats to work with a hanging grip, which carries over to every bar gymnastics skill.

exercises.name: Strict Toes-to-Bar
instructions: Hang completely still with straight arms and legs together.
Press into the bar with straight arms and lift the legs as straight as your flexibility allows.
Curl the hips up until both feet touch the bar.
Lower slowly to a dead hang without swinging.
exercises.formCue: No swing, straight arms, legs together.
exercises.commonMistakes: Using a swing to start the rep, or bending the arms to shorten the distance.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise straight legs to hip height only, or do strict hanging knee raises.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Taking the swing away builds the trunk strength and control that make the kipping version safe.

exercises.name: Knees-to-Elbows
instructions: Hang from the bar with straight arms and the shoulders active.
Press down on the bar and pull the knees up toward the chest.
Keep curling the hips until the knees touch the elbows.
Lower with control to a full hang before the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Curl the hips, knees meet elbows.
exercises.commonMistakes: Stopping at hip height, or swinging so much that momentum does the work.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise the knees to hip or chest height and build range over time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the bridge between a basic knee raise and toes-to-bar.

exercises.name: Single-Under
instructions: Hold a handle in each hand with elbows close to the ribs and hands slightly in front of the hips.
Turn the rope from the wrists, not the shoulders.
Jump just high enough for the rope to pass once, with a tall body and a soft bend in the knees.
Land on the balls of the feet and keep an even rhythm.
exercises.formCue: Small jump, quiet feet, wrists turn the rope.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jumping too high with a double bounce, or letting the hands drift wide so the rope shortens and trips.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the jump without a rope, tapping the thighs once per jump for timing.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A relaxed, efficient single bounce is the base that double-unders are built on.

exercises.name: Wall Walk
instructions: Lie face down with the feet against the wall and the hands under the shoulders.
Press up and walk the feet up the wall while walking the hands back toward it.
Keep the ribs down and the body tight until the chest is close to the wall.
Walk the hands out and the feet down under control until the chest is back on the floor.
exercises.formCue: Tight middle, small hand steps.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the lower back sag as the feet climb, or rushing the way down and dropping off the wall.
exercises.beginnerModification: Walk only part of the way up, stopping when the hips are above the shoulders.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It introduces being upside down while hands, feet and wall keep you supported.

exercises.name: Strict Handstand Push-Up
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, triceps, upper chest, traps, abs
instructions: Kick up to a handstand against the wall with hands just outside shoulder width and fingers turned out slightly.
Squeeze the glutes and abs so the body stays in one line.
Lower slowly until the top of the head touches the mat lightly in front of the hands, forming a triangle with the hands.
Press straight back up to locked elbows without resting on the head.
exercises.formCue: Head and hands make a triangle, lower like a feather.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping onto the head, or placing the head in line with the hands so the elbows flare and the press stalls.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do pike push-ups with the feet on a box so the hips sit over the shoulders.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds overhead pressing strength and balance with nothing but bodyweight.

exercises.name: Kipping Handstand Push-Up
instructions: Lower under control from the handstand to the head-and-hands triangle, keeping most of the weight on the hands.
Slide the hips against the wall and draw the knees down toward the chest.
Kick both feet straight up toward the ceiling.
Press hard through the hands as the legs extend and finish with locked elbows and a straight body.
exercises.formCue: Knees down, kick up, press.
exercises.commonMistakes: Crashing onto the head on the way down, or pressing before the leg drive so the kip adds nothing.
exercises.beginnerModification: Earn several slow strict reps first, and until then use box pike push-ups.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The leg drive lets you keep pressing overhead when strict strength alone would run out.

exercises.name: Box Step-Over
instructions: Stand facing the box with feet about hip-width apart.
Place one whole foot on top and drive through it to stand up on the box.
Step the other foot onto the box, then step down on the far side one foot at a time.
Turn around and repeat, leading with the other leg.
exercises.formCue: Whole foot on the box, push with the top leg.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pushing off the floor with the back leg, or letting the lead knee cave inward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a low step and hold nothing in the hands.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It gives single-leg strength and conditioning without the impact of jumping.

exercises.name: Burpee Box Jump-Over
instructions: Stand next to or facing the box and drop to the floor until chest and thighs touch.
Push up and bring both feet under the hips.
Jump onto or over the box and land softly with bent knees.
Step or hop down on the far side, turn, and start the next burpee there.
exercises.formCue: Chest down, feet under you, then jump.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jumping while still off balance from the burpee, or landing with stiff legs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step back and up in the burpee and step over a lower box.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It pairs getting off the floor with a jump, a hard test of conditioning and coordination under fatigue.

exercises.name: Bar-Facing Burpee
instructions: Stand facing a loaded barbell on the floor, square to it.
Drop down with the hands inside the plates until chest and thighs touch the floor.
Push up and bring the feet back under the hips.
Jump over the bar from two feet, land on two feet, then turn to face the bar again.
exercises.formCue: Face the bar, two feet up, two feet down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Drifting sideways to the bar, or stepping over one leg at a time when a two-foot jump is the standard.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step back and up in the burpee and step over the bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The fixed line to jump keeps every rep honest when you are tired.

exercises.name: Rope Climb
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, biceps, forearms, abs, hip flexors
instructions: Reach high on the rope with both hands and let it run down the outside of one leg.
Lift the knees, wrap the rope under that foot and over the top of the other, and clamp it between the feet.
Stand up on the clamp while reaching the hands higher.
Repeat the knees-up, clamp and stand until you reach the top.
Come down hand under hand while easing the foot clamp, never sliding.
exercises.formCue: Clamp with the feet, stand with the legs.
exercises.commonMistakes: Hauling with the arms alone because the foot lock slips, or sliding down and burning the hands and shins.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the foot lock from a seated box, or lower to lying and pull back to standing on the rope.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A secure foot lock turns the climb into leg work and saves the grip.

exercises.name: GHD Sit-Up
instructions: Sit on the glute-ham developer with the feet locked in and the hips just past the edge of the pad.
Lean back under control with a slight bend in the knees and the abs braced.
Go only as far as you can keep the lower back from over-arching.
Straighten the knees sharply and sit up until the hands reach the foot pads.
exercises.formCue: Brace going back, snap the knees to come up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Doing too many reps too soon, or relaxing the abs at the bottom so the lower back hangs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower only to parallel with the floor and keep the volume low for the first weeks.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the hip flexors through a long range while the abs learn to hold the spine steady.

exercises.name: GHD Hip Extension
instructions: Lock the feet in face down with the hip crease clear of the pad so the hips can bend freely.
Brace and set a flat, neutral back.
Fold at the hips and lower the torso while the back stays flat.
Squeeze the glutes and hamstrings to rise until the body is in one straight line.
exercises.formCue: Flat back, hinge only at the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding and unrounding the spine instead of hinging, or over-arching past a straight line at the top.
exercises.beginnerModification: Cross the arms on the chest and shorten the range, or do a bodyweight good-morning on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The hips do the work while the trunk holds still, the same demand as a deadlift.

exercises.name: Overhead Walking Lunge
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, shoulders, upper back, trunk
instructions: Press the weight overhead and lock the elbows with the arms beside the ears.
Step forward and lower until the back knee touches the floor lightly.
Keep the torso upright and the weight stacked over the shoulders and hips.
Drive through the front heel to stand and step straight into the next lunge.
exercises.formCue: Arms locked, ribs down, knee kisses the floor.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the elbows soften and the weight drift forward, or leaning the chest toward the front knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold one light dumbbell overhead with both hands, or lunge with no load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Holding a load overhead while the legs work shows up any weak link in shoulder and trunk stability.

exercises.name: Ring Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, rhomboids, rear delts, biceps, abs
instructions: Hold the rings with straight arms and lean back with the body in one line from head to heels.
Walk the feet forward to make it harder or back to make it easier.
Pull the chest to the rings with the elbows close to the ribs.
Lower until the arms are straight without letting the hips sag.
exercises.formCue: Body like a plank, chest to the rings.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping or thrusting the hips, or stopping the pull short of the chest.
exercises.beginnerModification: Stand more upright with the feet further back.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The angle is adjustable in seconds, so it builds pulling strength at any level.

exercises.name: Ring Dip
instructions: Hold a steady support on the rings with arms locked and the rings close to the hips.
Lower under control with the elbows tracking back and the rings kept near the body.
Go down until the shoulders are below the elbows.
Press back up to a full lockout and steady the rings before the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Rings tight to the body, finish locked out.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the rings drift wide, or cutting the depth and the lockout short.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the top support for time, or keep the feet on the floor or a band to take some weight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The unstable rings make the shoulders control the whole range, building strength a fixed bar does not ask for.
